newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast spot power falls despite nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast spot power falls despite nuke outage.

text.p: Most wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Northeast market fell sharply Monday from Friday's levels as the region began recovering from the most severe cold blast so far this winter season.
News of New York Power Authority shutting its 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 3 nuclear plant this past weekend failed to cushion the sharp price drop.
"It's not going to be a problem for the next couple of days," said a New York electricity trader, referring to the power availability in the state.
The generating unit in Indian Point, N.Y., was taken off line Saturday to repair its feedwater heaters.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Tuesday delivery in the eastern New York Power Pool (NYPP) tightened to $32.00-$33.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Friday's $30.00-$40.00 range for delivery today.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Tuesday in eastern NYPP was quoted $20.00-$22.00, compared with Friday's quote of $23.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Tuesday was valued at $24.00-$26.00, compared with Friday's $35.00-$40.00 for delivery today.

Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Tuesday plunged $5.00 to $15.00-$15.50 from Friday's $20.00. In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted $32.00-$34.00, compared with Friday's quote of $36.00 for today.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday at the NU border was assessed near $25.00, flat from Friday.

The relief from the chill, however, could be short-lived as another cold front was expected to arrive into the Northeast Friday. Temperatures ware expected to drop sharply from five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal to five to 10 degrees below normal Friday through Monday.
"I'm sure the (the market's) going to rebound if we see these temperatures," said the New York electricity trader.
Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said its 610 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point unit 1 in Scriba, N.Y., resumed full output over the weekend after shutting the plant Friday to repair a leak in the dry well.
New York State Electric and Gas Co's 650 MW Kintigh coal-fired station returned on line Sunday after tripping off line Thursday, market sources said.

Swing natural gas prices plummeted on the brief bout of mild temperatures. Spot gas values at the New York City gate fell more than $2.00 to $4.00-$4.25 per million British thermal units from Friday's $6.00-$6.50.
